title: Restriction of scalars commutes with $f^*$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]). For every morphism of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$ there is a
natural isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ f^*\;\cong\;f^*\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda'_Y}\longrightarrow\Mod_{\Lambda_X},
$$

with $f^*$ the pullback of module objects ([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]).

proof.text:
Put $F=f^*_{\Ab}$, the strong monoidal pullback on abelian sheaves supplied by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Write $\mu^F$ for its monoidal structure and $\gamma_M$ for the action on a $\Lambda'_Y$-module $M$. By the action formulas of [sk-def-sfb-transport] and [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], the actions on $FM$ obtained by first restricting along $a_Y$ and then transporting, or first transporting and then restricting along $Fa_Y$, agree:
$$
F\bigl(\gamma_M\circ(a_Y\otimes 1_M)\bigr)\circ\mu^F_{\Lambda_Y,M}
=F\gamma_M\circ\mu^F_{\Lambda'_Y,M}\circ(Fa_Y\otimes 1_{FM}).
$$
Here the equality is functoriality of $F$ followed by naturality of $\mu^F$. Both functors send a module morphism $h$ to $Fh$. Hence the identities of $FM$, with themselves as inverses, give a natural isomorphism
$\tau:\operatorname{mapMod}(F)\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{Fa_Y}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$.

proof.text:
Work in $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. Its tensor product is symmetric monoidal and closed, and tensoring on either side preserves colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Equalizers are formed sectionwise: the matching-family condition is preserved by taking the equalizer subgroup. Coequalizers are sheafifications of the sectionwise coequalizer presheaves, because the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies maps from these sheafifications to any sheaf with the maps equalizing the original pair. Thus the ambient hypotheses of [def-sfb-extend-comap-iso-of-iso] hold. Apply it with
$$
R=F\Lambda_Y,\quad S=F\Lambda'_Y,\quad R'=\Lambda_X,\quad S'=\Lambda'_X,
\qquad \varphi=Fa_Y,\quad\psi=a_X,\quad a=\alpha_f,\quad b=\alpha'_f.
$$
$F$ is strong monoidal as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. The rings $R$ and $S$ are commutative: $\Lambda_X$ and $\Lambda'_X$ are commutative because $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$ are ([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]), and $\alpha_f$, $\alpha'_f$ underlie isomorphisms of ring objects $F\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$, $F\Lambda'_Y\cong\Lambda'_X$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]), along which commutativity of the multiplication is transported. The square commutes by [lem-sfb-coefficient-pullback-square]. Its vertical sides $\alpha_f$ and $\alpha'_f$ are isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], applied separately to the arbitrary condensed rings $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$. The cited scalar-square construction therefore gives the natural isomorphism
$$
\sigma:\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha'_f}
\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{Fa_Y}.
$$
